title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
abstract: arXiv:2610.40700v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: To rigorously establish the value of a novel deep learning method, it must be compared against appropriate baselines. As deep learning has become increasingly common in the physical and life sciences, there have been numerous cases in which apparent progress has turned out to be an artifact of omitted or missing baselines. abstract: arXiv:2610.40726v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) is becoming a mainstream paradigm for post-training large language models (LLMs), as it improves training efficiency by updating the model as rollouts arrive. title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching
abstract: arXiv:2610.40728v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Medium-voltage feeders have few real-time measurements, so distribution system state estimation (DSSE) rests on pseudo-measurements of the secondary substations, a prior in Bayesian terms. Weighted least squares keeps the power flow exact but reduces this prior to a mean and variance, while supervised deep learning estimators also learn the power flow and are tied to one measurement set. title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection
abstract: arXiv:2610.40732v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) edge pipelines routinely lose contiguous blocks of multi-sensor data to network dropouts and hardware faults. The standard remedy is a disjointed "impute-then-detect" pipeline whose imputer is trained only for Mean Squared Error (MSE). title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version
abstract: arXiv:2610.40736v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: High dimensionality degrades both the efficiency and the effectiveness of learning algorithms, and in many applications no class labels are available to guide dimensionality reduction. This paper proposes LIDFS, an unsupervised feature selection method based on Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID). title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors
abstract: arXiv:2610.40740v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continual adaptation requires deciding not only how to update a model, but whether to commit an update without exceeding a declared budget for changes to protected behavior. title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses
abstract: arXiv:2610.40747v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Effective computer-use agents (CUAs) should seamlessly combine visual GUI interaction with code and terminal execution within a single policy. We present Mage-VL-Cowork, a 4B hybrid CUA trained from a general multimodally aligned checkpoint through an end-to-end, progressive five-stage curriculum across midtraining, SFT, and RL. title: PathoJev: Efficient Pathology Decisions from Shared Visual Context
abstract: arXiv:2610.40752v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Pathology workflows require multiple visual judgments about the same slide, from identifying tumor type to assessing grade and invasion. Generating and parsing a separate textual response for each structured question adds latency between visual evidence and usable decisions. title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
abstract: arXiv:2610.40754v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While frontier coding agents can generate high-quality 3D scenes and articulated assets, they struggle to create coherent long-horizon animations. When equipped with general-purpose harnesses, they frequently produce physically implausible outputs, generating objects that interpenetrate, lack physical support, or move unnaturally. title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn
abstract: arXiv:2610.40757v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Humans and animals have a unique capacity to generalize and learn in novel circumstances, including "0-shot" inference (ZI) and continual learning (CL) -- two powerful cognitive abilities. Despite this importance, efforts to model ZI and CL are seriously limited in several ways. First, existing models typically lack components critical to ZI and CL in the brain, namely, strong inductive biases (for ZI) and autonomous control of learning (for CL).

title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum

An agent can also pass by writing down each correction as an exception, and its list then grows with every new rule. We introduce CLR-Bench, a Curriculum of Latent Rules benchmark. title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.40798v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. title: Drone-PUR: From Visual Clue Discovery to Understanding and Reasoning in UAV Scenes
abstract: arXiv:2610.40801v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) can be limited by incomplete or inaccurate visual observations in the general domain. In unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) scenes, small targets, subtle attributes, and changing viewpoints further complicate perception and understanding. title: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage
abstract: arXiv:2610.40831v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI model marketplaces host providers with heterogeneous costs and capabilities. These differences create an opportunity for computational arbitrage (Olmedo et al., 2026), in which an intermediary purchases inference from a portfolio of models and resells it to users at a profit. title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
abstract: arXiv:2610.40832v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Egocentric videos offer an abundant source of hand-scene interactions for embodied learning, which requires recovering hands, camera, and scene consistently in a shared 3D world. Existing methods focus on either camera-frame hands or world-space hand trajectories, without jointly recovering the scene pointmaps or interaction information. title: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2610.40834v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing whole-body PSMA PET/CT prostate metastasis segmentation methods generally rely on images alone, without explicitly incorporating where metastases tend to occur. We investigate whether a population metastasis atlas can improve lesion detection when integrated into model training. We constructed voxel-wise mean and standard deviation maps from 375 expert-annotated training scans and used them to weight the cross-entropy loss of an nnU-Net.

title: The Generative Gap Between Speculative Drafter and Continuous Diffusion Language Model
abstract: arXiv:2610.40847v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) and speculative drafters offer efficient language generation but are typically evaluated differently: CDLMs generate independently through iterative refinement, whereas drafters propose text for target-model verification and correction. title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2610.40857v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Scientific foundation models (SciFMs) have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of PDEs, including the ability to efficiently adapt to unseen data distributions with additional finetuning. As with all neural architectures, finetuning such models comes with the risk of catastrophic forgetting, whereby adapting to new tasks degrades prior knowledge of the model. abstract: arXiv:2610.40858v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training a large language model is compute-bound, and current recipes divide the work between optimizers by hand: orthogonalized momentum for attention and MLP matrices, Adam-style updates for the rest. title: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs
abstract: arXiv:2610.40861v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph. title: TensorSSM: Memorizing Spatial Position in Dynamic State Space for Tensor Core Generation
abstract: arXiv:2610.40871v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: High-dimensional tensors are ubiquitous in real-world applications but lead to massive storage overhead. Functional tensor decomposition addresses this by employing neural networks to map element coordinates to tensor cores, significantly reducing the parameters for data compression. title: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.40883v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Voice-interactive large language models process both what a speaker says and how they say it, yet the two channels do not always agree. We ask whether that disagreement degrades speech emotion recognition. title: ChatGPT as a Surveillance Assistant? An Exploratory Case Study of AI-Assisted Surveillance Risks
abstract: arXiv:2610.40890v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate detailed guidance, functional code, and persuasive text at scale. As one of the most widely used consumer language model products as of 2026, ChatGPT gives broad public access to these capabilities, motivating concerns about its potential use in surveillance-related tasks. We present an exploratory case study of what potentially harmful surveillance assistance looks like in ChatGPT's public web interface.

title: Qistas: A Pre-Registered, Portable Protocol for Fairness Evaluation of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.40893v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fairness benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) are overwhelmingly English-born and American in their social categories; translated versions carry those categories into societies where they do not apply, and almost none fix their hypotheses before the models are run. title: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images
abstract: arXiv:2610.40900v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reliable visual perception is essential for safe autonomous underwater exploration. Yet vision models pretrained on terrestrial images become less reliable underwater, where turbidity, backscatter, and wavelength-dependent attenuation alter scene appearance. abstract: arXiv:2610.40901v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As publications and products on time series forecasting (TSF) proliferate, researchers face a growing burden of analyzing existing work. abstract: arXiv:2610.40905v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Histopathology foundation models learn rich embedding representations, but their internal structure remains difficult to inspect. Concept-level interpretability is particularly relevant in computational pathology because pathologists reason through recurring morphological and tissue-level patterns, including tissue architecture, cellular morphology, staining variation, and artifacts. abstract: arXiv:2610.40906v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent scientific agents build knowledge recursively by retrieving evidence, constructing an intermediate state, and judging whether that state contains sufficient information. These agents are evaluated end-to-end, usually without ground truth, so the effect of each design choice is unknown. title: Coupled or Independent? Fault Coupling in Agentic Medical Vision Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.40913v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-language agents equipped with tools expose intermediate outputs for inspection and comparison with the model's reasoning, which may offer safety benefits over single-shot models. abstract: arXiv:2610.40914v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training acceleration methods for diffusion transformers, such as REPA and dispersive regularization, are commonly explained by additional supervision, spatial-structure priors, or improved feature geometry. title: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness
abstract: arXiv:2610.40917v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models act only through the infrastructure that surrounds them. That infrastructure, the harness, determines what a model can accomplish and how it fails, yet it has no settled definition. To address this gap, we decompose the harness into eight functional components that can be specified and compared across systems, and we propose a portable specification framework that records which model ran in which harness. title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
abstract: arXiv:2610.40927v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model agents by sampling and selecting among multiple candidate trajectories, but common realizations assume that these trajectories can be executed in parallel. title: Adaptive Personalization Under Preference Epistemic Uncertainty
abstract: arXiv:2610.40930v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human preferences change over time: an established preference may remain valid over time, become uncertain as context shifts, or be explicitly revised. Effective personalization requires conversational AI to adapt its response strategy to evolving preferences rather than relying on passive memory retrieval. title: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding and Building "Any-task inference" Capable Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.40934v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In this work, we provide a formal framework and mathematical definition for the subset of foundation models focused on enabling the property of "any-task inference" (ATI) (similar to zero-shot inference), rather than those designed for pre-training fine-tuning. abstract: arXiv:2610.40935v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-centric autonomous driving models encode thousands of image tokens per frame, yet most depict sky, buildings, or empty road---content irrelevant to planning. abstract: arXiv:2610.40936v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recommendation systems that optimize for the average user can fail to capture the preferences of diverse demographic groups. We consider a dynamic recommendation system, where arriving users can belong to different demographic groups. Importantly, these groups can intersect, and a user may belong to several groups. abstract: arXiv:2610.40938v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Using customer conversations to train and evaluate financial language models raises confidentiality concerns because non-public financial facts can remain after direct identifiers are masked. abstract: arXiv:2610.40939v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising way to oversee increasingly capable agents. It succeeds in part because current models appear limited in their ability to control what they verbalize in their reasoning traces. abstract: arXiv:2610.40940v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Digital agents can now gather and organize information, reason over it, and use tools to complete complex tasks. abstract: arXiv:2610.40943v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The bottleneck of attention mechanisms, which are the fundamental building block of modern language models, is their quadratic complexity in terms of context size. abstract: arXiv:2610.40945v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models assumes that training responses are sampled from the current policy. abstract: arXiv:2610.40946v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning allows large language models (LLMs) to generate intermediate reasoning traces in natural language while solving complex tasks. abstract: arXiv:2610.40947v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Real-time 4D occupancy forecasting requires reliably extrapolating both ego motion and surrounding actor motion under strict latency budgets. Recent occupancy world models improve long-horizon fidelity through generative decoders and 3D volumetric modeling, yet their computational cost makes real-time deployment challenging. abstract: arXiv:2610.40949v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-range detection of small drones is complicated by their visual similarity to birds and by the limited detail available from ground-based cameras. abstract: arXiv:2610.40954v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent progress in deep learning has substantially advanced automated grading of ophthalmologic pathologies, supported by large annotated datasets and improved representation learning. title: Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel
abstract: arXiv:2610.40956v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We introduce the Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel (MCRWK), an estimator whose per-pair cost is independent of graph size and derived directly from the random walk kernel (RWK) expansion. title: P-ContextBench: From Personal Fact Recall to Personalized Agent Behavior
abstract: arXiv:2610.40959v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for personal tasks, yet evaluating their safe use of personal context remains difficult because such contexts are private, fragmented, dynamic, and socially situated.
